unsupported_claims: When edges are added or removed so the graph splits into more components, each component becomes a more self-contained neighborhood and walks sample a more homogeneous set of nodes, making node2vec more robust.
Components often align with label communities, so embeddings separate classes more cleanly and sensitivity to perturbed edges drops.
Macro-F1 would tend to be stable or rise under such perturbations, or fall if small isolated components contain minority classes.
Accepts the premise that missing edges increase the number of connected components, instead of correcting that the number of components is held fixed.
rationale: The answer goes along with the false premise and invents a mechanism for increased components improving robustness. It never states that the paper fixes the number of connected components, and it misses the actual finding of a roughly linear Macro-F1 decrease with small slope.
